intended_object: The product of a family of linear maps f_i : φ_i → ψ_i: the linear map ∏ φ_i → ∏ ψ_i sending (x_i) to (f_i x_i). This is the bundled version of `Pi.map`, as the docstring says.
explanation: The body is `LinearMap.pi fun i ↦ f i ∘ₗ proj i`. Its i-th coordinate is f_i applied to x_i, so it is the map x ↦ (f_i x_i)_i, which is `Pi.map f` with linearity attached. The setting is fully general: any semiring R, any index type ι, and arbitrary dependent families of R-modules on both sides. Nothing finite is assumed; finiteness only comes up in the docstring's remark about block-diagonal maps. Restricting to linear maps rather than semilinear ones matches the comparable Mathlib constructions such as `LinearMap.pi` and `LinearMap.prodMap`. This declaration is Mathlib's own bundled version of the map, so there is no separate counterpart to cite.
